The capstone — answering "what is the ultimate, never-surpassed medium":
a topological property, not a quality bar. A medium is unsurpassable iff
every improvement is a move WITHIN it (no outside from which to build a
successor). First-light (mentl2.wat == mentl3.wat) is the smallest
instance of that fixed point — the medium reproduced exactly by itself.

- §9.1 the five collapses (assert→prove, represent→project,
  know→not-know, now→always, one mind→many) are one pattern: a distance
  prior media charged the human to cross by hand, driven to zero because
  the two sides are one graph read two ways. The medium raises the human
  by carrying everything that was never thinking.
- §9.2 the rung past μ: the medium projects BECOMING — the graph's own
  evolution (edits, proofs, Reasons, across minds, across time) as a
  cursorable graph — not only STATE. "Programming language" dissolves
  into "language"; that is why language design is never surpassed.
- §9.3 NFre is the grain of sand: the last monomorphization-era binary
  in the kernel. Under uniform-i32, type is a capability on the gradient,
  not a precondition for existence.

strengthened with the fixed-point line.
mentl/64f9ae2:
parse_fn_stmt previously short-circuited to parse_block directly when
body started with `{`, returning a BlockExpr without invoking
binop_loop. Trailing `~>` operators were left unparsed — the wheel's
canonical pipeline form

  fn compile_stdin() = {
    read_stdin() |> frontend |> ... |> emit_module
  }
    ~> wat_stdout
    ~> wasi_filesystem
    ~> ...

parsed as `fn compile_stdin() = { ... }` with `~>` chain dropped on
the floor, leaving every perform site inside the body with an empty
lower-stack at lower-time and falling through to LConst(0).

Fix: always route fn body through parse_expr. parse_expr dispatches
`{` to parse_block via parse_primary, then binop_loop picks up
trailing pipes — the chain becomes one PipeExpr tree, lower_pipe
pushes each handler onto the stack BEFORE lowering body, and perform
sites inside body resolve to discriminated handler arm fns.

Empirical: tiny test case `fn main() = { perform wat_emit("hello") } ~> wat_stdout`
now emits `(call $op_wat_stdout_wat_emit ...)` directly. TLet
multi-line indented bodies retain the dedicated parse_implicit_body
path (let-stmt is statement-position not expression-position, so
parse_expr's primary dispatch does not handle them).

Eight interrogations: parser layer projecting AST forward through
the pipe topology (Graph), parse_expr is the residue (Handler), `~>`
draws the topology (Verb), no row change (Row), structural ownership
(Ownership), no refinement at parse time (Refinement), structural
gradient — handler chain visible on the page IS the projection
(Gradient), Reason chain via PipeExpr's recursive shape (Reason).

Drift refused: 9 (parse_block direct-call was a deferred-by-omission
of pipe continuation in fn body position; now lands whole), 6
(no special-case for `{` body shape — uniform parse_expr dispatch).

Closes task #125. Cascade-companion to task #124 (tail-call mark
pass) — together they unlock perform-resolution in handler-chained
fn bodies for L1.

mentl/64476d4:
The H4 walkthrough's addendum named the gap: a record/variant's
effective region is the JOIN (deepest = innermost = max region_id)
of its alloc site and every embedded pointer field's region. Without
this, escaping the record to outer scope orphans inner-region
pointer fields.

Substrate (types.ka):
  RegionTrack gains tag_alloc_join(value_handle, field_handles).
  tag_alloc remains for scalar/leaf allocs (closures and effect
  alloc returns); composites take the joining path.

Implementation (own.ka):
  region_tracker's tag_alloc_join arm computes the join: for each
  field handle, look up its tagged region (untagged → 0 = global);
  pick the max across (current_region, all field regions); stamp
  the composite with that region and the install_span.

  join_field_regions helper does the max-fold over the field list.
  Field handles that aren't in tagged_values (scalars never
  pass through tag_alloc) contribute 0 — global lifetime, doesn't
  bound the join.

Sweep (infer.ka):
  MakeListExpr → tag_alloc_join(handle, collect_handles(elems))
  MakeTupleExpr → tag_alloc_join(handle, collect_handles(elems))
  MakeRecordExpr → tag_alloc_join(handle, record_field_handles(fields))
  NamedRecordExpr → same
  CallExpr (constructor) → tag_alloc_join(handle, collect_handles(args))

  record_field_handles helper extracts value handles from
  (name, value_node) field tuples.

LambdaExpr stays on tag_alloc (no embedded pointer fields — the
captures-as-record IS the closure shape, but captures are scoped
to the closure's lifetime by definition; the closure can outlive
its captures only via incorrect lower bounds, which is W4 evidence
territory, not field-region territory).

Walkthrough alignment: H4 addendum's "Field-store as escape vector"
section. The join logic is what the addendum proposed; it lands as
a single new effect op + a single helper, the substrate-native
shape.

turbosort/64c3415:
The parallel sort re-read the whole array every pass to rebuild per-chunk
histograms, and allocated a zeroed scratch buffer like the old serial
core. Compute every pass's per-chunk histograms in one up-front parallel
scan; their sum is the global count and their first-pass slice is reused
directly as the first scatter's per-chunk offsets, so the first pass skips
its rescan. Use the wide-digit path for 8-byte keys, scatter into
uninitialized capacity, and copy back in parallel. About 1.24x at 10M u32
over 0.1.1 under identical conditions.

A fused variant that accumulated next-pass histograms during the scatter
was measured slower -- the per-element accumulation competed with the
scatter's random writes for cache -- and rejected; the module docs keep
the result so it is not retried blindly.
clob/64626ac:
Adds src/nn/confidence.rs with ConfidenceHead — a linear probe with the
same shape as EnergyCritic (Head N) but an independent weight vector and
no internal baseline/Weber logic. Training target is per-step NLL,
identical to Head N, but the separate parameters prevent gradient
cannibalization when both heads learn from the same signal. predict()
clamps at zero since NLL is non-negative; train_step() is the same MSE
primitive Head N uses.

CoreModel gains an optional confidence head, a NoveltyDetector wrapping
its outputs for adaptive thresholding, an AdaptiveConfig, and an
extra_steps_counter. When adaptive_config.enabled is true and Head C's
detector z-score on the predicted NLL exceeds z_threshold, the block
stack iterates up to max_extra_steps additional times on the current
buffer before unembedding — the poor-man's pondering loop. The
NoveltyDetector's 10-step warmup behavior (z=0 until calibrated)
naturally suppresses adaptive firing before Head C is meaningful, so
there's no special-case warmup guard needed.

Callers drain the extra-step counter via take_extra_steps() after each
decode. cmd_ingest records each extra step into the metrics window,
surfacing it in the clob-metrics dashboard as a new column.

New calibrate-confidence subcommand mirrors the existing calibrate
command but trains ConfidenceHead against NLL and writes a separate
side-file. Ingest picks the head up via --confidence-head, and
--adaptive-compute / --adaptive-max-extra / --adaptive-z control the
pondering loop.

tokensafe/64ab145:
detectLpLock only recognized known locker programs (Streamflow/UNCX), so LP
burned to the Solana incinerator (1nc1nerator…) — the dominant 'lock liquidity'
pattern on memecoins — showed up as a non-locker top holder and was wrongly
penalized as 'unlocked' (a false rug signal on actually-safe tokens). Treat the
incinerator as a permanent lock (locker name 'Burned (incinerator)'): LP sent
there is unspendable, so the dev can never pull it. Scoped to the verified
incinerator pattern; deliberately did NOT guess PumpSwap pool layouts (no
empirical RPC verification available) to avoid frail safety-critical code.
